description: We are Team AgroNova, a group of beginner BCA students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in agriculture, space science, and technology. Although we are beginners and do not have much coding experience, we are eager to learn new skills, explore innovative ideas, and work together to solve real-world agricultural challenges using NASA data.
summary:
We developed Field Shift Advisor, an interactive agroecological decision-support system that empowers smallholder farmers to transition from vulnerable monoculture to climate-resilient, soil-regenerative crop rotations.

The tool addresses the challenge by integrating live NASA POWER satellite agroclimatology data—including precipitation, temperature extremes, and root-zone soil moisture—with local crop traits and farmer-measured rainfall observations. Our agronomic engine dynamically evaluates candidate rotations across seasonal water balance, biological nitrogen fixation, pest cycle disruption, and heat stress thresholds. It bridges coarse satellite grid estimates to micro-field realities through a farmer-in-the-loop rain-gauge calibration model and provides interactive precipitation stress-testing from -50% to +30%.

This project is vital because smallholder agriculture underpins global food security yet suffers disproportionately from erratic weather patterns, topsoil erosion, and escalating input costs. By transforming complex NASA Earth observations into transparent, actionable cropping calendars with quantified evidence and localized risk warnings, Field Shift Advisor delivers accessible, science-backed guidance to protect yields, replenish soil health, and safeguard rural farming livelihoods.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? How is your project creative? What factors did your team consider?

What it does and how it works

Field Shift Advisor is an interactive web-based agroecological decision-support system designed to help smallholder farmers shift from static monoculture to resilient, soil-regenerative crop rotations.

The application works in four integrated steps:

  1. Interactive Geospatial Selection: Users select their farm location on an interactive Leaflet map (or enter latitude/longitude coordinates).
    • Effective Water Balance: Seasonal rainfall plus 30% antecedent soil moisture versus crop water demand.
    • Heat Stress Risk: Frequency of extreme temperature months (Tmax⁡≥33∘CT_{\max} \ge 33^\circ\text{C}Tmax​≥33∘C) weighted by crop heat tolerance.
    • Soil Regeneration: Incentivizing biological nitrogen fixation (N2N_2N2​ fix) and botanical family alternation (e.g., Cereal →\rightarrow→ Legume) to suppress pest/disease cycles.
    • Erosion & Fallow Protection: Identifying bare fallow months with ≥50 mm\ge 50\text{ mm}≥50 mm rainfall and auto-scheduling Sunhemp green manure cover crops.
  2. Actionable Results: The interface presents the top 3 ranked rotation plans, a visual 12-month cropping calendar, dual-axis climate charts, explicit agronomic reasoning, quantitative evidence, and local risk warnings.

What benefits does it have?

  • Restores Soil Health: Encourages nitrogen-fixing legumes that naturally rebuild organic matter and reduce expenditures on synthetic fertilizers.
  • Breaks Pest & Disease Cycles: Systematically rotates botanical families, cutting off continuous host availability for soil pathogens and pests.
  • Curbs Topsoil Erosion: Auto-schedules fast-growing green manure cover crops in high-rainfall fallow windows to prevent erosion and nutrient runoff.
  • Interactive Climate Stress-Testing: Features a rainfall adjustment slider (-50% to +30%) so farmers can simulate severe drought or heavy monsoon scenarios before planting.
  • Explainable Transparency: Provides clear agronomic rationale, data evidence, and localized risk disclosures rather than opaque "black-box" scores.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to protect smallholder farmer livelihoods and food security in the face of erratic rainfall and climate shocks:

  • Economic Resilience: Shields vulnerable smallholders from catastrophic single-crop failures and volatile agrochemical prices.
  • Agroecological Regeneration: Rejuvenates degraded drylands by boosting soil biodiversity, moisture retention, and nitrogen levels.
  • Empowering Extension Services: Serves as a digital decision aid for local agricultural extension agents, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and farmer cooperatives.
  • Sustainable Development Goals: Directly advances SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.10+, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Backend Architecture: Flask 3.0 (lightweight, modular REST API).
  • Satellite Data & APIs: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (daily/monthly precipitation, temperature, root-zone wetness).
  • Database: SQLite3 (embedded storage for regional crop profiles, satellite cache, rain-gauge logs, and saved plans).
  • Frontend & Mapping: Leaflet.js with OpenStreetMap geospatial tiles; Chart.js for responsive dual-axis climate and rainfall trend charts.
  • Hardware Requirements: Runs on standard consumer laptops or low-power edge computers, requiring zero dedicated GPUs and minimal memory footprint.

How is your project creative?

  • Fusing Satellite Data with Rain-Gauge Ground Truth: Solves the classic satellite resolution dilemma (~50 km grid) by empowering smallholders to calibrate satellite baselines with simple on-farm rain gauge observations.
  • Automated Ecological Gap Filling: Rather than just suggesting a single following crop, the system dynamically scans the entire annual calendar and automatically inserts Sunhemp green manure cover crops during rainy fallow intervals.
  • Interactive "What-If" Climate Simulator: Transforms static satellite archives into a dynamic, reactive climate simulation tool that lets farmers test their rotation's viability under simulated drought or excess rain.
  • Humble, Explainable Decision Support: Rather than acting as an infallible authority, the system explicitly communicates data evidence, identifies missing variables (e.g., micro-terrain slope), and alerts users to check with local agronomists before planting.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Digital Divide & Intermittent Connectivity: Rural agricultural areas frequently experience poor internet connectivity. We integrated local 30-day SQLite caching and an offline climatological fallback so the application works seamlessly even if NASA APIs are unreachable.
  • Zero Cost & Open Access: Avoided paid third-party APIs, proprietary frameworks, and compulsory user logins so any farmer, student, or extension worker can use the tool freely.
  • Holistic Agronomic Realism: Evaluated crops across ecological, hydrological, and risk factors rather than maximizing short-term yields alone.
  • Local Scientific Grounding: Acknowledged that satellite data cannot observe local soil texture or field slope; built-in disclaimers mandate field-level corroboration with local agricultural universities and extension offices.
